verified.rule: His ToS "Small Caps Volatile Scan": scan in All Stocks; Last ≤ $100; Volume ≥ 1,000,000; % change vs the prior close ≥ +25%; show 50. No float, cap, short-interest, RVOL or relative-strength filter.
verified.numbers: price ≤ $100 · volume ≥ 1,000,000 · change ≥ +25% vs prior close
quotes: the price of the stock anything from 50 cents to $100 … volume should be minimum 1 million volume and then percentage change from the previous day at least minimum 25% change

verified.rule: Price FLOOR: $0.50 in every source dated on or before 2024-01-17; on 2024-02-01 he lowered it to $0.10.
quotes: There’s no fixed lower amount, Nazmi. I saw PHUN (0.2$ stock) ran good the other day and I couldn’t see it as my scanner was screening 0.5$ and above. So, I brought the scanner to show me 0.1$ and above
verified.contradiction: the two videos say 50 cents; his later post says $0.10 — DECISIONS 2026-10-13 uses his latest, $0.10

verified.rule: Premarket: exactly two scanners — the Zendoo live YouTube scanner and his custom ToS premarket scan (≥ 1M volume, ≥ +25% since the last close; no price band stated for it).
ToS built-ins always open: Pre-Market Movers sorted by volume; % Gainers (after the open) sorted by % change; no thresholds.
quotes: ThinkorSwim has this pre-market movers scanner … I sort by volume
verified.contradiction: Business Insider's ">25% premarket" on the default scanner is a conflation of his two scanners

verified.rule: Volume: 1M is a floor, "the more the better"; it must SUSTAIN and INCREASE (one 1M bar then a fade = not interested); no RVOL multiple anywhere.
quotes: the minimum is 1 million volume in my scanner … the more the better
the volume is sustaining and it's increasing … this gradual increase in volume catches my attention

verified.rule: Float: "the lower the float the better"; GG gives NO cutoff; he reads it from the ToS "Shares" column (generally shares outstanding). The "<10M float" / ">20% SI" labels are Zendoo panel titles, not his.
quotes: the reversal squeeze happens only in the low float stocks, the lower the float the better
verified.note: status is about the NUMBER: no source gives a float cutoff

verified.rule: Float rotation: examples only (PO ~1–2M float, ~4M shares in the first 5-min bar; BS 624K float, 60M volume — watched, not traded).
Catalyst: a "must", but never researched; 100% technical → no news/catalyst gate (F4VS's "require a catalyst" is wrong as a filter).
quotes: I'm a 100% technical trader … I don't look at the news much … I just trade the price and volume action

verified.rule: Long only, stocks only, intraday; no shorts, options or futures; no overnight holds in low floats; no leverage on small caps.
quotes: I only do long side trading, I don't short.

verified.rule: Short interest: no threshold and no short-interest filter in ANY source.
Past runners and 2nd-day plays are watched; daily wicks / prior violent moves are "simply added confluence … not a requirement"; no relative strength.
Mid-day new names are ignored if notable names formed earlier.
verified.contradiction: tension with S9 25:39 "YouTube scanner will show me what's new"

verified.rule: Scan output ~20/10/5 names (F4VS) vs 5–8 a day (Business Insider) — not a gate.
verified.contradiction: F4VS's Q&A (S2) says ~20 on the scan, 10 watchable, 5 very good; Business Insider says five to eight a day; GG gives no count

verified.rule: Watchlist 12–15 names, 4–5 active (1–2 in poor markets), up to 18 charts.
His day starts 06:30 CT = 07:30 ET; he scans until the open, then builds watchlists.
"Prepare 30 minutes before the open" (F4VS) — not his schedule; not encoded.
verified.contradiction: his own post: the day begins at 06:30 CT and he scans until the open

verified.rule: Prior-day after-hours movers stay on the morning watchlist; focus lists 1/2/3; "whatever is very active and close to my setups I'll have in top priority monitor".
quotes: there will be some stocks which make after hours moves from the past day, I'll keep them as well

verified.rule: Watchlist admission = "increasing gradual volume, and slow pullbacks".
"I usually don't take trades for the first 15 minutes after the market opens" (his 2023 data says the whole first HOUR is his worst).
quotes: I usually wait for the first 15 mins after the market open.

verified.rule: Very little premarket trading; outside regular hours: limit orders only, less size.
quotes: limit orders only … slippage … I trade with less size after and pre-market

verified.rule: A huge premarket sell-off: not watched actively; he re-engages only if demand returns after the open and a setup forms.
quotes: If there’s huge sell off, I don’t watch it actively and if the demand picks up after or later market opens, I’ll see how the price and volume unfolds and enter if there’s a setup. Else no trade.

verified.rule: Watches into the close; trades the last two hours when an after-hours move is building.

Post-market: a per-trade journal written AT ENTRY (ticker, risk, setup grade, discipline grade, patience grade, then how he sold); evening review; screenshots of every trade AND misreads into Google Slides; weekly analysis.
Weekend: ToS OnDemand replays of the BIG movers he traded or missed (video only those; screenshots of all), Camtasia, Drive; a weekly game plan.
verified.contradiction: scope: the masterclass says "all trades"; his later X reply and the webinar say big movers only

verified.rule: After a big run: "a couple of days" of noise, then it fades; after a 1,000%+ runner he watches "the next one two weeks"; he demotes a name to a low-priority third-monitor list when there is no setup all day + volume drying + a slow fall (the host coined "graveyard"; GG agreed).
verified.note: the 2-session stay-listed number on the tab is Ajay's (DECISIONS), not GG's

verified.rule: Meditation is a PRE-market habit when nothing is moving.
quotes: if there is no action I'll go meditate

verified.rule: Situational awareness = counting the day's runners: a good day = "four five" at 100%+ (a 400%, a 300%) + a bunch at 80–90%+; a bad day = best runners 30–40%, the rest 10–20% → trade light or not at all; 40–100% is undefined.
SPY/QQQ do not filter his small-cap trading (bottom-up).
Pop & Drop: several names failing to hold breakouts → smaller size until the market picks up (no numbers).
A+ setups: 1–2 a week in bad markets, ~1 a day in good ones.
Decay, 2024-10-11: his setups stopped appearing for long stretches and worked far less often.
quotes: I do not see my setups for very extended periods and even if I see one, the probability of it working drastically reduced.

verified.rule: 5-minute primary, 15-minute secondary; 1/2/3/10-minute tried and rejected.
quotes: I tried 1 minute 3 minute 5 minute 15 minutes … I concluded on the five minute

verified.rule: Only indicators: the 9 EMA and 21 EMA on the close; "my chart has nothing else" (no VWAP, ADR or level 2).
quotes: Always the 9 EMA and 21 EMA.
I don't use level2 at all

verified.rule: The EMAs run through the shaded pre-market bars on two of his ToS screenshots (RVSN, VCIG) — a visual reading, never said in words.
verified.note: a reading of his ToS screenshots — the images carry no webinar timestamp (S8 25:36 only names the two EMAs), so no ts is filed

verified.rule: VolumeAvg length 50 on one of his layouts (RVSN) vs 5 on another (VCIG) — a pane default, not a stated rule.
verified.note: the tab's 50-bar volume average is Ajay's choice (DECISIONS); a reading of his ToS screenshots — the images carry no webinar timestamp (S8 25:36 only names the two EMAs), so no ts is filed

verified.rule: His charts are in Central Time (+1 h → ET).
F4VS's "Horizontal Fade 30m / Kiss & Fly 5–15m / Bull Flag 5m (and 1m)" — GG names only 5m and 15m, shows zero 30m examples and rejects 1m.
verified.contradiction: third-party frames vs his own "five and 15 minutes"

verified.rule: Daily chart: draws support/resistance, checks squeeze history; "when the daily and the intraday have the congruence … the probability is always high"; no numbers.
Psychological $1 / $5 / $10 = profit-taking / climax levels (sold TPST into $10; expected a climax stall at $5).
verified.note: the 5% 'near' band on the chip is Ajay's number, not GG's

verified.rule: Psychological levels as ENTRY triggers — he called the 5.05 entry FOMO ("I shouldn't have taken this trade") and the 1.04 entry "not the perfect execution".
verified.contradiction: entries at $1 / $5 were his own named mistakes

verified.rule: Most profitable hours in 2023: 11 AM and 5 PM ET; the first hour was the worst; "one year of data is a small sample size".
OHLC bars, not candles (habit) — display only.
quotes: This is how I learnt when I started trading. I'm more comfortable with this approach. Old habits :)

verified.rule: "most of all these setups have the same criteria: good demand, very shallow pullback with low volume and very constructive action … if it takes this previous highs enter and stop loss would be of the base" — the very next sentence introduces the Reversal Squeeze as a different structure.
verified.contradiction: a single shared stop disagrees with his per-setup stops

verified.rule: "My style and playbooks all revolve around the same pillar: … price compression after a big advance."
quotes: My style and playbooks all revolve around the same pillar: I’m interested in stocks that show a price compression after a big advance.

verified.rule: Volume dries up at the entries of all his setups and picks up if the setup works.
quotes: The volume will dry up during the entries of all my setups and it picks up if the setup works.

verified.rule: Pullback volume is judged RELATIVE to the advance bars ("considerably low compared to these green bars"), not as a bar-by-bar decline.
Pole: at least 2 big green bars (3 is better), price and volume rising gradually.
quotes: at least two big green bars (three is good) with a good price increase

verified.rule: Flag: sideways or very shallow near the top of the last green bar, on lower volume.
quotes: almost sideways or very shallow pullback with less volume compared to the left side
verified.note: the 0.50 depth / 0.50 volume numbers are Ajay's (K3)

verified.rule: Flag length: "usually … two to three bars", BUT his own valid masterclass example "took five bars to the side"; the F4VS examples ZYNE and NXTP took 5 and 4 pullback bars.
quotes: the pullback is one bar, usually two to three bars
verified.note: 1–3 = A+, 4–5 = 'long flag' (listed, never pushed) is Ajay's K4a

verified.rule: Volume step: "twice, thrice" the previous candle is fine, ~10× = climax / invalid; 3–10× is never stated; the baseline is the PREVIOUS candle.
Invalid: one big candle (NVCT); two sudden bars + a first pullback that gives back too much (RKDA); heavy pullback volume; a downtrend.
Uptrend with the 9/21 EMAs rising.
Entry = the high of the pullback bar, stop = its low; careful variant = the higher of two close highs / the lower of the two pullback lows.
quotes: entry at the top of the pullback bar, exit [stop] at the bottom of it
verified.contradiction: anchor: Business Insider's NXTP fill entered at $2.40 through the pole high $2.39 with the stop $2.01 at the flag low (S12 2024-02)

verified.rule: The fastest setup: it happens within ~10 minutes and takes off.
quotes: it happens within 10 minutes and takes off, this is the fastest

verified.rule: Reclaiming the highs within 2 bars = extra strength (ICCT).
Takes the 1st and 2nd flag, usually skips the 3rd (Business Insider only).
A low-volume flag (PXMD ~200K) → reduced size.
Bull Flag and Kiss & Fly have his highest win rate (no numbers).
quotes: Setups 1 and 2 (bull flag and EMA kiss and fly)

verified.rule: Four points: good demand (the left side can be just 1–2 green bars), an organic pullback, low pullback volume, price kisses and HONORS the 9 EMA, often repeatedly ("touch and go").
quotes: only two green bars or one green bar … it waits more and honors the 9 EMA whenever it pulls back

verified.rule: Entry = the high of the kiss bar, stop below the low of the previous bar; careful: the prior highs if close, the pullback low as the stop.
"≥ 2 EMA [reversals]" (Business Insider) — he took NEXI as an A+ with ZERO touches.
quotes: the fact that price didn't even touch the EMA let me think that it might have a very explosive move
verified.contradiction: BI's two-touch minimum vs his own zero-touch A+

verified.rule: His HKD example has 9 sideways low-volume pullback bars he counted himself.
~30 minutes to decide vs 10–15 for the Bull Flag (descriptive).

Good demand, less selling than buying; sideways around the top of the highest price action or a small dip on low red volume; selling decreases gradually; honors the 9 EMA, then drifts onto the 21 EMA as volume nearly dries; "by the end … the 9 EMA, 21 EMA almost meet", then momentum starts.
quotes: when the 9 EMA and 21 EMA merge around that area then slowly the momentum starts

verified.rule: A larger, longer base — "not something that happens very often".
Entry "once you see it takes the new highs … this would be my entry" / "enter it at the top of this price action"; stop "the low of this one" / "below the previous bar".
5-minute and 15-minute ("looks even better in 15min"); a 30-minute frame is unsupported.
quotes: If I flip to 15 minutes it looks even better.

verified.rule: Invalid: an impatient early entry (BWV 2022-05-09).
The lowest-volume bar right before the move — said about the strong-demand slow fader (this setup), "like a vcp characteristics too".
quotes: volume completely dried out and the price is not going down … then it makes a big move
verified.note: STRATEGY_SPEC §1.4 attribution fix: this is Horizontal Fade, not Intraday VCP

verified.rule: Left-side demand ("even one bar is fine"); the pullback on LOW volume ("This is a must"); support at the 21 EMA, not the 9 ("this is not a strong momentum setup"); higher lows; each cycle shrinks in price AND volume volatility.
quotes: it honors the 21 EMA when it pulls back with less volume … in each cycle it honors the 21 EMA and the volatility contracts in each cycle

verified.rule: Entry at the "top of the previous cycle highs" when it is "almost very calm and silent", stop "the bottom of it".

His own examples tolerate imperfection: "Not completely honors the 21 EMA … but it does these higher lows" (valid); "expanded in the volatility in the second cycle … but still it took off"; "Not a perfect one but, good to include it in the playbooks".
verified.note: the 'B — imperfect' listed read is Ajay's answer (never pushed)

verified.rule: Invalid: heavy selling after the main bar (LQR), a sharp drop with no higher lows (AYLA), sideways chop with no prior uptrend.
Base-on-base = higher probability; a big runner that goes sideways on less volume and forms another base has a high chance of an even bigger move.
quotes: if it moves sideways with less volume and forms another base, high chance it has an even bigger move

verified.rule: Business Insider's "21-day EMA" = the 21-PERIOD EMA on the 5-minute chart (reporter mislabel).
Low float only ("the lower the float the better"); GG gives no number — "<10M" is Business Insider's own sentence.
verified.note: the 10,000,000 cap on the tab is Ajay's (K8)

verified.rule: Strong demand; drops snap straight back ("like a ball under the water", "tennis ball action"); it has tried to squeeze in earlier bars and been sold; this time the sell-off is big and the recovery quick.
quotes: whenever there is a drop it tries to squeeze up, whenever it hits the ground it [reverses] hard
this time the sell-off was big and the [reversal] was quick
verified.note: the 8% / 2% / 3-bar numbers and the failed-attempt rule are Ajay's (K8, H1, H2)

verified.rule: Typical session: sells off at the open, reverses, goes sideways at the top as volume fades, then explosive.
quotes: at the morning open it tried to sell off completely and then bumps up and waits and then makes explosive move

verified.rule: Entry = takes the highs after the quiet base; stop = the base low.
Tends to squeeze into the close or after hours.
quotes: most of the stocks make a big move after hours

verified.rule: Invalid (F4VS): a spike-and-decline too violent (SNES), a steady fade (SASI), no demand after the open (SGD).
An undercut of the base is acceptable (answer to a leading question).
Shorts are forced to buy — no short-interest number anywhere.
quotes: when it squeezes, all the short sellers have to convert to buyers

topics.topic: Traits that are NOT setups (chips / Playbook, never entries)

verified.rule: Next-day / multi-day mover: "this is not kind of setup but … a characteristics" — previous-day strength + a big after-hours move; next day he enters only if a setup forms; his on-screen example was a failed one.

Halts: a halt-up = "too much of demand in the short very short time", typical of low float; he does not ENTER while it is halting up and down — "when it's clean, when it's calmer, then I enter"; once IN a trade a halt-up raises his confidence.
Confluence: 2–3 setups in one chart (e.g. a daily reversal + an intraday bull flag) = "the certainty of the move is higher"; no weight, no count rule.

After-hours squeeze: holds strength into the close → the after-hours run is "much smoother, the volume will be low, but … the magnitude … huge"; exhaustion: "when the intraday action is so big … it won't run that big in after hours"; he lost twice going big after hours expecting a repeat.
"Classic momentum breakout" (CGC, 2024-03-27): gradual push, contraction on lower volume around the 9 EMA, breakout on good volume; entry 7.3, stop the prior-bar low 7.1 — NOT one of the five.
Red flags before entry: "more than 3 red closes is red flag to me => wait more"; a big-volume bar closing at half its range = selling; demand immediately sold = wait.
After a stop-out on a big high-volume seller: "Mostly pass and wait more"; no re-entry on the next bar, "at least like couple of bars".

topics.topic: Entry / stops / exits / risk — his discretion, NOT computed

verified.rule: Enters "right at the break" intrabar by default; sometimes waits for the bar close; "no hard rule, will depend on the strength and candle size".
quotes: No hard rule, will depend on the strength and candle size.

verified.rule: Market orders in regular hours (entries and stops); limit orders only outside regular hours.
The stop is known before entry; "almost all my setups will have low of the prior bar as the stop loss"; he exits before the stop on hesitation; a breakout back into its range = out.
quotes: most of my exits [stops] are below the low of the previous bar, always

verified.rule: Breakeven once it moves; add the second half at ~zero risk.
Partials of 1/3 or 1/2 into strength after ~15 min / 3 bars when strong; trail along the 9 EMA (the 21 on Kiss & Fly "maybe"); in drawdowns take half off immediately.
Base counting: the 3rd base → climax, peel early; the 4th base → out (one example); counter-rule: 100% then a quiet sideways base → a bigger leg.
No fixed targets ("sometimes 3:1, sometimes 10:1").

Risk: he STARTS at 0.25% of the account per trade (his own starting risk) and moves it with MONTHLY performance; progressive exposure; raise only on a cushion that survives 2 losers; a −10% / −15% drawdown → the next five trades ≤ −5% together; A+ up to double; all-in only on an obvious A+ with a cushion.
verified.contradiction: the "5% to 10%, then 2.5%, 2%" figure at S8 1:47:23 has an AMBIGUOUS basis (position vs risk) — never presented as a risk %; the spec's "B+ = 2% risk 'medium size'" clause is NOT carried: at S9 33:57–34:23 he puts a medium-size position at "10 20%" of the account — a position share, not a risk %, so that basis is AMBIGUOUS too

verified.rule: Business Insider's "exit a loser within five minutes" is a reporter's line; his own 2023 numbers say losers average ~10 minutes.
quotes: My avg hold time is 1hr for winners and 10 mins for losers.

verified.rule: Dollar Wisdom's "exit everything on a close below the 21 EMA, 3 setups" — never implemented.
verified.contradiction: not in any first-hand source; his exits are discretionary (E5)

verified.rule: 2023 USIC +805.1%, stock accounts under $1,000,000.
2023 full year: 745 trades, win 31% / loss 68%, average winner +8.55%, average loser −4.06% → expectancy 0.31 × 8.55 − 0.68 × 4.06 = −0.11% per trade.

2nd half of 2023: 165 trades, win 28%, average winner ~+13%, average loser ~−4% → 0.28 × 13 − 0.72 × 4 = +0.76% per trade. The 805% came from SIZE (all-in on A+), not per-trade edge — never quote 805% as a setup's expectancy.
Holds: winners ~40–60 minutes, losers ~10 minutes.
quotes: My average hold time of winners is ~40 mins

verified.rule: Q1 2024 +35.02% (a promotional post).
Stopped teaching on 2024-05-15.
quotes: I’ll be stop teaching at Momentum Access from May 15th due to health issues.

verified.rule: October 2024: year-to-date "only in double digits", trading "almost none".
quotes: Overall YTD is +ve but only in double digits.
